why.stone: Faceted bold and numerals paired with chiselled Roman capitals read most convincingly as letters cut into stone.
why.carving: One coherent faceted language runs through the lowercase, the capitals with their long Q tail, and the digits; the cuts are crisp and the 0 and O are clearly distinct.
why.calm: The lighter, open capitals are dignified and steady while the bold keeps its presence.
why.personality: The mix of Roman capital proportions and polygonal chisel facets is a distinctive, recognisable voice.
why.inscription: Wide round O, C and D against narrow E, S and B with a measured rhythm give classical inscriptional proportions, close to Trajan or Cinzel with a cut finish.

why.stone: Its chiselled bold faceting and cut caps read as hewn stone while staying controlled.
why.carving: Crisp, consistent cuts across caps, lowercase and digits, and the caps feel part of the same design, though the carved bold digits sit beside an uncarved regular set.
why.calm: Bold presence with a measured rhythm; nothing feels aggressive.
why.personality: The faceted bold with its classical caps (including the long-tailed Q) has a recognisable character.
why.inscription: The ss01 caps are wide-round and lighter than K1's, with a classical Q tail and a dignified rhythm close to Roman inscription.

why.stone: Faceted bold and numbers plus flared, wedge-serifed ss01 capitals read clearly as inscription in stone.
why.carving: Cuts are crisp and digits distinct; the flared ss01 capitals are a slightly different idiom from the faceted lowercase, but they still belong together.
why.calm: Calm, dignified presence; the lighter ss01 weight keeps the capitals from shouting.
why.personality: Carved lowercase combined with glyphic flared capitals and the long Q tail make it memorable.
why.inscription: Wide round O C, narrow E S R, flared glyphic terminals and an even rhythm give the most convincing Roman inscriptional capitals of the set.

why.stone: Faceted, chiselled bold weights and heavy wedge-serif capitals feel hewn and grounded, though the regular titles stay a fairly conventional book serif.
why.carving: The faceted cuts are crisp and consistent across bold lowercase, capitals and digits (0 vs O distinct), but the ss01 capitals are a much heavier, blockier voice than the regular lowercase, so they read slightly pasted on.
why.calm: Steady and grounded, but the very heavy ss01 SISIFO block gets close to shouting.
why.personality: The polygonal facets give it a recognisable stonecut voice without being gimmicky.
why.inscription: The capitals are sturdy, but E, B and S are wide and heavy, so the proportions read more as a slab-like wedge serif than classical Roman lettering.

why.stone: Faceted, chiselled bold weights and the wedge-cut caps read convincingly as hewn letters while the regular stays grounded.
why.carving: The cuts are angular and deliberate and shared by caps, lowercase and digits, though the bold 62.5 looks slightly rough beside the smooth regular 147.5.
why.calm: It has strong presence in bold without shouting, and the regular weights are steady.
why.personality: The faceted bold and the heavy cut SISIFO give it a recognisable voice.
why.inscription: The ss01 caps are wide and dignified with round O and C, close to Roman proportions, though the heavy bold SISIFO leans more poster than lapidary.

why.stone: Faceted, polygonal bowls on bold text, numbers and capitals give a clear hewn-stone feel without losing the serif base.
why.carving: Facets are applied consistently across lowercase, capitals and digits, and 0/O, 1/7, 3/8 stay distinct, though the heaviest bold counters look slightly lumpy.
why.calm: Steady, well-weighted presence; the heavy ss01 SISIFO is assertive but not shouting.
why.personality: The chiselled polygon curves give a recognisable voice on top of a familiar book serif.
why.inscription: ss01 capitals are wide with round O C and narrower E S, giving a dignified inscriptional rhythm, but serifs stay bookish rather than Roman-cut.

why.stone: It shares the hewn, faceted bold and numerals, and the condensed capitals look like a carved plaque.
why.carving: The cuts are clean and deliberate and the digits are clear; the condensed ss01 capitals are coherent with the facets but their proportions break from the lowercase.
why.calm: The tall, narrow capitals are quiet and upright with presence, and nothing is aggressive.
why.personality: The condensed faceted capitals give a distinct, slightly archaic poster voice.
why.inscription: Everything is uniformly condensed (narrow O, C and D), the opposite of classical inscriptional width contrast.

why.stone: It has the same faceted chiselled bold, and the carved caps feel cut into stone.
why.carving: Cuts are coherent across caps, lowercase and digits, and the digits are clearly distinct.
why.calm: It is calm and present, though the condensed caps add some vertical tension.
why.personality: The carved facets are distinctive, but the condensed caps make it read more like a generic condensed titling face.
why.inscription: The ss01 caps are narrow and condensed, so O, C and D are not wide and the rhythm is far from classical Roman proportions.

why.stone: Same faceted, hewn treatment as K1, so bold display reads as cut stone.
why.carving: Cuts are coherent across cases and digits stay distinct, though the condensed ss01 capitals compress the facets into tighter, busier shapes.
why.calm: Composed and readable; the condensed capitals feel a little tense but not aggressive.
why.personality: Distinct carved voice, with the tall condensed capitals adding an upright, slightly Germanic note.
why.inscription: ss01 capitals are condensed with narrow O and C, the opposite of classical Roman proportions.
